title: Measurement of the reduced dipole matrix element in Ba$^+$
authors: N. Jayjong, M. D. K. Lee, K. J. Arnold, M. D. Barrett
abstract: We present a high-precision measurement of the reduced electric-dipole matrix element $\langle P_{1/2}\|r\|S_{1/2}\rangle$ in $^{138}\mathrm{Ba}^+$. By comparing off-resonant scattering rates with dispersive Stark-shift measurements, we determine the matrix element to be $3.322\,7(12)$, corresponding to a $P_{1/2}$ excited-state radiative lifetime of $7.866\,3(56)$~ns. Combining our experimental results with a prior model for the differential scalar polarizability $Δα_0(ω)$, we extract the static value $Δα_0(0) = -73.09(12)$a.u. This determination directly improves the evaluation of the blackbody radiation (BBR) shift, minimizing a prominent systematic limitation in room-temperature $\mathrm{Ba}^+$ optical clock error budgets. These results provide a stringent benchmark for atomic-structure calculations and advance high-precision applications in quantum metrology and tests of fundamental physics.
summary: This paper reports a high-precision, experimental determination of the reduced electric-dipole matrix element for $	ext{Ba}^+$ using trapped ions. By meticulously comparing scattering rates and Stark shifts, the authors significantly improve the calculated value for the static differential scalar polarizability. This advancement directly reduces systematic uncertainties in room-temperature optical clock error budgets.
main_problem: The primary goal is a high-precision measurement of the reduced electric-dipole matrix element $\langle P_{1/2}\|r\|S_{1/2}angle$ in singly ionized barium ($	ext{Ba}^+$). This measurement aims to improve the accuracy of calculating the Blackbody Radiation (BBR) shift for optical clocks.
main_result: The authors determined the reduced dipole matrix element to be $3.3227(12)$ and extracted a static differential scalar polarizability $\Delta\alpha_0(0) = -73.09(12)$ a.u., significantly improving clock error budgets.
method: The measurement combines off-resonant scattering rate measurements with dispersive Stark-shift measurements on the $S_{1/2} - P_{1/2}$ transition in $	ext{Ba}^+$. The ratio of these rates is used to extract the matrix element while suppressing systematic errors.
model_or_system: The experiment uses trapped $	ext{Ba}^+$ ions, probing transitions between $S_{1/2}$, $P_{1/2}$, and other levels. The analysis relies on rate equations describing population dynamics under the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA).
key_observables: Reduced dipole matrix element $\langle P_{1/2}\|r\|S_{1/2}angle$, scattering rates ($\gamma_s$), and Stark shifts ($\Delta s$).
important_parameters: The measurement is highly sensitive to systematic effects like polarization imbalance, Zeeman shifts, and detuning imbalances; these are quantified and minimized.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of rate equations derived under certain approximations (e.g., first order in small parameters) and carefully accounts for various systematic shifts by comparing measurements at different conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the level structure, timing sequences for measurements, and plots showing the measured matrix element versus detuning, confirming consistency across measurement settings.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup using $	ext{Ba}^+$ ions, describes the methodology involving interleaved Stark-shift and scattering-rate measurements, presents the data analysis to extract the RME, and concludes by applying this result to improve BBR shift calculations for optical clocks.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of precision measurement in atomic physics. The techniques used—combining time-resolved population dynamics with Stark shifts—are central to quantum optics and developing next-generation atomic clocks.

FIG. 3. Timing sequences for Stark shift measurements (left) and scattering measurements (right). Clock pulse for the scattering measurements represents that total time for the six separate pulses discussed in the text.

FIG. 4. Measured matrix element ⟨P1/2∥r∥S1/2⟩as a function of ∆. The raw experimental measurements are shown as blue circles and the data corrected for Stark-shift contributions from other levels are shown as red squares. Error bars on all data points represent ±1σ uncertainties. The solid blue line represents a linear fit to the raw data. The fitted y-intercept, 3.322 7(12) ea0, yields the matrix element value that cancels leading order corrections to the Stark shift given by Eq. 1. The horizontal solid line indicates the overall average value, while the surrounding dashed lines mark the corresponding ±1σ experimental statistical uncertainty.

FIG. 5. Half the measured population differences when scat- tering from either m-state of S1/2 at both t0 and t1 at each of the four detunings used in the measurements. The statistical agreement with zero supports the negligible effects of residual deviations from linear polarization or Zeeman shifts.
